sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Financials stand out as the sole sector with clean, multi-timeframe breadth, while Technology and Energy maintain their grip on absolute momentum leadership.

Technology (momentum 0.82) and Communication Services (momentum 0.45) are the week's sole positive rotators, each gaining +1 spot to reach rank 2 and rank 9, respectively. Energy (momentum 0.70) remains highly competitive at rank 1. Meanwhile, the Financial sector (momentum 0.65) exhibits the healthiest underlying breadth in the market, standing as the only group to register positive performance across all measured timeframes (week, month, quarter, half, and YTD).

On the downside, defensive and cyclical laggards continue to lose ground. Utilities fell -1 spot to rank 10 with a weak momentum score of 0.17, while Consumer Cyclical remains anchored at the bottom of the board at rank 11 (momentum 0.35). Basic Materials is also showing signs of exhaustion, dropping -1 spot to rank 3 despite its otherwise strong momentum profile.

## Strength
* **Financials Stand Alone:** Financials (momentum 0.65, rank 7) is the only sector out of 11 to achieve "all-green" status, showing positive performance across the week, month, quarter, half-year, and YTD.
* **Tech and Energy Anchor the Top:** Technology (momentum 0.82) and Energy (momentum 0.70) continue to lead the market in absolute momentum, holding the rank 2 and rank 1 YTD positions respectively.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Tech and Telecom Rising:** Technology (+1 spot, rank 2) and Communication Services (+1 spot, rank 9) were the only sectors to improve their momentum rankings over the last 5 sessions.
* **Utilities and Cyclicals Dragging:** Utilities fell -1 spot to rank 10 with a weak momentum score of 0.17. Consumer Cyclical (momentum 0.35) remains the lowest-ranked sector at rank 11.
* **Industrials Stalling:** Despite holding a relatively high YTD rank of 4, Industrials has faded into the momentum laggards category with a weak score of 0.38.

## Divergences
* **Basic Materials Fading:** Basic Materials is flagging an early warning sign; despite high overall momentum of 0.67, it slipped -1 spot to rank 3 over the last 5 sessions.
* **Value vs. Growth Split:** Financials show the most robust breadth (all-green) yet sit at rank 7 YTD, while higher-ranked sectors like Basic Materials (rank 3) are actively losing momentum.

rotation_phase.reasoning: Energy and Basic Materials are leading as top year-to-date performers alongside Technology, while defensive sectors like Healthcare lag, aligning with classic late-stage economic expansion.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Heavy industry and energy commodities dominate market leadership, led by Oil & Gas Refining and Coking Coal, while consumer-facing retail and renewable utilities suffer sharp near-term pullbacks.

Market breadth remains highly concentrated, with only 17 of 143 industry groups achieving "all-green" status. Energy and industrial services continue to anchor the top of the board; Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing leads all groups with a momentum score of 0.94, while Coking Coal (+15 spots to rank 47) and Software - Infrastructure (+16 spots to rank 64) drive the strongest positive rotations, signaling a dual bid for cyclical commodities and select tech infrastructure.

Conversely, consumer-linked sectors and green energy are fading rapidly. Specialty Retail plunged 28 spots to rank 104, and Apparel Manufacturing fell 22 spots to rank 105. Momentum remains thoroughly depressed in Footwear & Accessories (0.05) and Solar (0.13), while previously resilient segments like Diagnostics & Research (momentum 0.74) and larger energy plays like Oil & Gas E&P (momentum 0.66) are showing early signs of momentum fatigue, both slipping 5 spots in rank over the last five sessions.

## Strength
* **Concentrated Breadth:** Only 17 of 143 industry groups are "all-green" (positive across week, month, quarter, half, and YTD periods), highlighting a narrow market leadership.
* **Refining & Commodities Dominance:** Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing holds the market's highest momentum score of 0.94, maintaining sustained strength alongside Marine Shipping (0.85) and Staffing & Employment Services (0.87).
* **Sustained Leaders:** Biotechnology, Diagnostics & Research, and Software - Application join the top-performing commodity groups as sustained leaders over 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top Gainers:** Software - Infrastructure led the 5-day rank improvements (+16 spots to rank 64, momentum 0.78), closely followed by Coking Coal (+15 spots, rank 47, momentum 0.88) and Consumer Electronics (+15 spots, rank 42, momentum 0.69).
* **Sharp Declines:** Specialty Retail dropped 28 spots to rank 104 (momentum 0.20), while Utilities - Renewable fell 23 spots to rank 108 (momentum 0.19).
* **Deep Laggards:** Footwear & Accessories (0.05) and Airports & Air Services (0.07) anchor the bottom of the momentum rankings, showing no signs of recovery.

## Divergences
* **Fading Leaders:** High-momentum groups are beginning to lose ground, with Shell Companies (momentum 0.61) slipping 10 spots, and Diagnostics & Research (momentum 0.74) and Oil & Gas E&P (momentum 0.66) both dropping 5 spots.
* **Emerging Defensive Rotation:** Low-momentum defensive groups are starting to climb in rank, led by Utilities - Diversified (+8 spots, momentum 0.35), Household & Personal Products (+6 spots, momentum 0.45), and Utilities - Regulated Gas (+6 spots, momentum 0.33).
